text:
alex: Customer reports SSE sessions repeatedly drop after ~15s. They get a partial chunk, client reconnects in a tight loop, and billing spikes. Logs show repeated write errors from our side.

sami: Which customer + region? any repro steps yet? :thinking:

alex: acme-marketing, us-east-1. Repro steps in their app: open SSE /v1/stream?session=... send initial ~3KB system context, then idle. After ~12-18s they see partial JSON then `ERR_CONNECTION_RESET`. They sent server logs: 

```
2026-03-15T18:12:07.412Z INFO sse: accept conn id=0x7f9a
2026-03-15T18:12:22.129Z WARN sse: writev returned EAGAIN, bytes=0 conn=0x7f9a
2026-03-15T18:12:22.129Z ERROR sse: write retry 1/3 delayed flush conn=0x7f9a
2026-03-15T18:12:22.139Z ERROR sse: write retry 2/3 delayed flush conn=0x7f9a
2026-03-15T18:12:22.149Z ERROR sse: write abort after max retries conn=0x7f9a reason=backpressure
2026-03-15T18:12:22.150Z INFO sse: connection closed remote=10.2.3.45:51122
```

alex: customer also pasted kernel counters: `tcp_sndbuf` spiked to 131072 and stayed.

nina: Do we see our internal slow-consumer metric incrementing? Which path aborts the connection?

josh: The code path is `sse/streamer.go:flushLoop` — we treat repeated EAGAIN as fatal after `maxWriteRetries` (default 3) and then call `conn.forceClose()`. That was intended as a safety but it might be too aggressive for noisy mobile clients or flaky proxies.

shruti: I repro'ed locally with a netcat client that stops reading after the first event. Behavior: server attempts to flush, gets EAGAIN, retries 3x, then we abort. Pipe shows socket sndbuf stayed full.

```
# simple repro (bash)
{ echo -ne "GET /v1/stream HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\nConnection: keep-alive\r\n\r\n"; sleep 0.2; } | nc localhost 8080 >/dev/null &
# stop reading -> simulate slow consumer
sleep 1; # server sends initial events then hits EAGAIN
```

shruti: From a customer-facing perspective, recommend two short-term workarounds: 1) client keepalive/read loop every 5s, 2) reduce initial burst size (<1KB). That keeps server drainability.

alex: Customer asked for a timeline and root cause. They said billing shows many short lived streams which they didn't expect.

mitchell: I'm going to escalate to eng-sre. Proposed immediate mitigation: increase `maxWriteRetries` to 8 and emit a metric `sse.write_retries` + alert on abnormal retry rates. For long-term: implement graceful backpressure pause (pause writer, mark stream as "slow-consumer", don't immediately abort).

josh: Agree. Also add metric for `sse.sndbuf_full` and log the peer info so we can correlate with client IP and proxy. We should NOT change retries in prod without deploying to staging first.

nina: I'll open a dedicated canary rollout (staging -> 5% -> 100%) for the change. We'll also include a tracing header to correlate requests.

alex: Customer wants a repro bundle. I'll send them a small node snippet to reproduce and a temporary config to bump retries on their dedicated instance.

```
// node repro (client)
const http = require('http');
const req = http.request({ host: 'api.redwood', path: '/v1/stream', headers: { 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' } }, res => {
  res.on('data', chunk => {
    console.log('got', chunk.length);
    // intentionally stop reading after first chunk to repro
    // remove this handler to avoid slow-consumer
    process.exit(0);
  });
});
req.end();
```
ingest-bot: tag:customer:acme-marketing severity:high component:sse attached:logs/2358004321.tar.gz

sami: next steps?

mitchell: assigning to eng-sre (pager: @oncall-sre). I'll create a support ticket with the proposed mitigation and timeline. If we can reproduce in staging we'll roll the retry bump there and monitor `sse.write_retries` and `sse.connection_closes_reason=backpressure`.

alex: thanks all — keep me posted, customer is waiting for ETA. :thumbsup:
